result:
I fixed the unsubscribe function in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, the one used to detach handlers. I haven't run the test suite.

**Cause:** `subscribe()` never changes the handler set in place. Each new subscription copies the set, adds the new handler and stores the copy. But the detach function it returned deleted the handler from the copy made at subscribe time. Once any later subscription had replaced that copy, detaching removed the handler from a set nothing reads any more, so the handler stayed attached. Every re-attach then stacked another copy of the webhook, audit-log and usage handlers.

In-app notifications never doubled because `notification-service.ts` attaches its handlers once when the module is imported. The register and detach cycle doesn't touch them, and they keep working while the other handlers are detached.

**Fix:** detaching now reads the current set, copies it without the handler and stores the copy, the same way subscribing works. After this:
- every detach and re-attach cycle ends with exactly one copy of each handler;
- while handlers are detached, no webhooks, audit rows or usage increments are produced;
- registering again without detaching is still a no-op, because of the existing check in `registerEventHandlers()`.
